title: Diljit Dosanjh to Perform at Latin Grammy Awards in Las Vegas on November 12
excerpt: The Latin Recording Academy added the Punjabi singer to the 27th annual ceremony at the MGM Grand Garden Arena, alongside Karol G and Bizarrap — watchable in the US on Univision and ViX.
body:
• Diljit Dosanjh, the Punjabi-language singer and actor, has been confirmed as a performer at the 27th Latin Grammy Awards on November 12, 2026.
  • The ceremony is at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas; the Latin Recording Academy announced the latest performer list on November 5.
  • He joins a lineup that includes Karol G, Bizarrap, Bad Gyal, DJ Premier and Grupo Niche in the new additions, and Rosalía, Anitta and Daddy Yankee among those announced earlier.
  • In the US, the three-hour telecast airs on Univision, UNIMÁS and Galavisión and streams on ViX from 8 p.m. ET/PT (7 p.m. CT), with a pre-show an hour earlier.

Punjabi music has a slot on one of Latin music's biggest stages. Diljit Dosanjh will perform at the 27th Latin Grammy Awards at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on November 12, the Latin Recording Academy confirmed in its latest performer announcement on November 5, according to Pollstar's report of the announcement. Dosanjh's team reacted to the Academy's Instagram announcement with the comment his fans would expect: "Punjabi AA Gaye Grammy Oye" — Punjabis have arrived at the Grammys — as Mirchi reported.

The lineup he joins

The November 5 additions also include Karol G, Jay Wheeler, Bad Gyal, Baby Ranks, Bizarrap, Miguel Colón, Divino, DJ Premier, Grupo Niche, Lil Supa, Luis Enrique, Nathy Peluso and Ángel "Cucco" Peña. Previously announced performers for the 27th annual ceremony include Rosalía, Carín León, Anitta, Mon Laferte, Grupo Frontera, The Warning, Xavi, Cristian Castro, Feid, Jorge Drexler and Daddy Yankee, who is also being honoured as the Latin Recording Academy's Person of the Year. The three-hour telecast includes a special tribute to the late Willie Colón, the trombonist, singer and composer who pioneered the salsa movement, with Ennio Gatti gathering Colón's original 13-member band to honour his legacy.

"Dosanjh's team reacted to the Academy's Instagram announcement with the comment his fans would expect: "Punjabi AA Gaye Grammy Oye" — Punjabis have arrived at the Grammys — as Mirchi reported ."

How to watch from the US

The awards ceremony airs live on Univision, UNIMÁS and Galavisión and streams on ViX beginning at 8 p.m. ET/PT (7 p.m. CT), with a one-hour pre-show from 7 p.m. ET/PT. For the diaspora reader, that is the complete watch path: no separate India broadcast is needed to see the performance live from Las Vegas.

The ceremony will be hosted by Roselyn Sánchez, returning as host for the tenth time, according to reports of the announcement, and the Academy's site, LatinGrammy.com, carries the full performer and nominee lists. Dosanjh's inclusion stands out in that company for a simple reason: the Latin Grammys are built around Spanish- and Portuguese-language music, and a Punjabi-language performer is not a booking the ceremony makes by routine. His team's one-line reaction treated it as a breakthrough rather than a booking, and the diaspora audience that has followed his rise from Punjabi cinema and music to international festival stages is likely to read it the same way.

A busy fortnight for Dosanjh

The Las Vegas date sits inside a crowded tour schedule. Dosanjh is currently on his Aura India Tour, which began with a concert in Delhi on October 30, and his next India performance after the Grammys is scheduled for November 15 in Indore, according to The CSR Journal's report. The Latin Grammy performance itself — what he performs has not been announced — is the news: a Punjabi-language artist on the Latin Recording Academy's main stage, in a lineup otherwise drawn from Latin music's own stars.
